quizName: DMV Practice Test #16 25 Questions • Passing Score 20

questions.question: When carrying a passenger, which of the following do you NOT need to adjust?
questions.explanation: A motorcycle sits lower when carrying a passenger due to extra weight. You may need to adjust tire pressure, suspension, shocks, headlights, and mirrors. You do not need to adjust brake light position.

questions.question: What is the best footwear for riding a motorcycle?
questions.explanation: Wear sturdy shoes that cover and support your ankles. Short heels are best because tall heels may catch on surfaces. Tuck in laces so they do not catch on anything.

questions.question: What should you do when riding in rain or fog?

options.text: Switch between low and high beam headlights

questions.explanation: Use your low beam headlight in rain, snow, or fog. High beams can reflect off these conditions and make it harder to see.

questions.question: How high above the seat can motorcycle handlebars be?
questions.explanation: In Vermont, motorcycle handlebars must be no more than 15 inches above the seat.

questions.question: How should you position your motorcycle in a lane?

options.text: Stay in the same spot in the lane at all times
Change your position based on road and traffic conditions
Always ride in the center of the lane
Ride in a zigzag pattern so drivers notice you

questions.correctAnswerText: Change your position based on road and traffic conditions
questions.explanation: No single lane position is always best. Change your position as needed based on road and traffic conditions.

questions.question: How much stopping distance do motorcycles need compared to cars in traffic?
questions.explanation: Motorcycles need the same stopping distance as cars in traffic.

questions.question: How do you do maximum straight-line braking?

options.text: Use the front brake first, then the rear brake
Use the rear brake first, then the front brake
Use both front and rear brakes at the same time without locking either wheel
Use both brakes at the same time while locking the rear wheel

questions.correctAnswerText: Use both front and rear brakes at the same time without locking either wheel
questions.explanation: Apply both the front and rear brakes at the same time without locking either wheel to stop in a straight line as quickly as possible.

questions.question: How much more likely is a helmeted rider to survive a crash?
questions.explanation: Riders without helmets are three times more likely to die from head injuries in a crash than riders wearing helmets.

questions.question: What should you remember when going through a curve?

options.text: Always stay in the same part of the lane
Always stay in the left part of the lane
Always stay in the right part of the lane
The best path may not follow the curve of the road

questions.correctAnswerText: The best path may not follow the curve of the road
questions.explanation: Road and traffic conditions change. Be ready to change your lane position as needed. The best path through a curve may not match the curve of the road.

questions.question: What does a linked braking system do?

options.text: Connects the front and rear brakes, applying both when either brake lever is used
Connects the front brake to the gear shifter
Connects the rear brake to a foot control
Connects the rear brake to a handlebar switch

questions.correctAnswerText: Connects the front and rear brakes, applying both when either brake lever is used
questions.explanation: A linked braking system connects the front and rear brakes. Using either brake applies pressure to both brakes. Check your owner's manual for details about your motorcycle's braking system.

questions.question: How much of a motorcycle's stopping power comes from the front brake?
questions.explanation: The front brake is stronger than the rear brake. It provides at least 70 percent of the motorcycle's total stopping power.

questions.question: What should you do when a vehicle passes you from behind?

options.text: Move to the center of your lane.
Move to the left side of your lane.
Move to the right side of your lane.
Do not worry about where you are in the lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: Move to the center of your lane.
questions.explanation: Ride in the center of your lane when being passed. Staying too close to the passing vehicle increases the risk of a crash.

questions.question: Under normal conditions, what is the minimum following distance for a motorcycle?
questions.explanation: Under normal conditions, keep at least two seconds between you and the vehicle ahead. Increase this distance if road or traffic conditions are poor.

questions.question: How should a group of motorcyclists ride when entering a highway or curve?

options.text: On the far right side of the lane

questions.explanation: Use single-file when turning, taking curves, or entering or exiting a highway. A staggered formation is better on straight roads.

questions.question: Who sets the pace for a group of riders?
questions.explanation: The last rider sets the pace. This ensures no riders are left behind.

questions.question: What should you do when riding through turns?

options.text: Turn your head and shoulders to look through the turn
Keep your knees away from the gas tank
Turn only your head and eyes to look through the turn

questions.correctAnswerText: Turn only your head and eyes to look through the turn
questions.explanation: Look through the turn toward where you want to go. Turn only your head, not your shoulders. Keep your eyes level with the horizon.

questions.question: What type of sign is rectangular in shape?
questions.explanation: Regulatory signs such as speed limit signs are rectangular with white background and black lettering. You must follow the rules on these signs.

questions.question: How do you achieve maximum braking power in a straight line?

options.text: Use the rear brake while downshifting

questions.explanation: Apply both the front and rear brakes fully without locking either wheel to achieve maximum braking power. Always use both brakes when slowing or stopping.

questions.question: What is the minimum following distance when riding at night?
questions.explanation: At night, it is harder to see and judge distances. Keep at least three seconds between you and the vehicle ahead. You need extra time to see a stopped vehicle and to slow or stop.

questions.question: Where should inexperienced riders be placed in a group?

options.text: In the front of the group
At the back of the group

questions.explanation: Inexperienced riders should ride near the front, just behind the leader. Experienced riders can watch them from behind.

questions.question: What color are warning signs with black lettering or symbols?
questions.explanation: Warning signs are yellow with black lettering or symbols. They tell drivers about upcoming road conditions.

questions.question: If you must brake and swerve to avoid a hazard, what should you do?

options.text: Brake first then swerve, or swerve first then brake.
Brake and swerve at the same time.
Choose to either brake or swerve.
Do not swerve and only use the front brake to stop.

questions.correctAnswerText: Brake first then swerve, or swerve first then brake.
questions.explanation: Do the actions one at a time—either brake then swerve, or swerve then brake. Do not brake while swerving because this can cause your motorcycle to fall over.

questions.question: A person of legal drinking age with a blood alcohol concentration (BAC) of ______ is considered legally intoxicated.
questions.explanation: For people of legal drinking age, a BAC of 0.08 percent or higher is legally intoxicated. Riding a motorcycle while intoxicated is illegal and dangerous.

questions.question: What guarantees that another driver sees you?
questions.explanation: Nothing guarantees another driver sees you. It is safest to assume that if another vehicle can enter your path, it will.

questions.question: If your front tire locks while braking, what should you do?

options.text: Keep the brake engaged until you stop completely.
Release both brakes and coast to a stop.
Release the brake lever and use only the rear brake.
Release the brake lever until the tire grips the road again.

questions.correctAnswerText: Release the brake lever until the tire grips the road again.
questions.explanation: If your front wheel locks while braking, release the brake lever until the tire grips the road again. Then apply the brake again.
